candidates.title: Measure and bound allocator fragmentation on the fak-native Qwen3.8 serve path

hard_gates.name: bounded-source-coverage
hard_gates.evidence: allocator input is retained once outside vLLM-IR

hard_gates.name: semantic-merge-integrity
hard_gates.evidence: fragmentation is a residency/lifetime mechanism, not an IR or lowering spelling

hard_gates.name: fak-native-execution
hard_gates.evidence: allocation, residency, scheduling, cache, and recovery remain fak-owned

hard_gates.name: end-to-end-witness
hard_gates.evidence: long-running receipt reports reserved/live bytes, quality, throughput, and recovery

hard_gates.name: no-llama.cpp-fallback
hard_gates.evidence: llama.cpp is reference/borrow evidence only, never fallback

frame.for: operators sustaining variable-shape Qwen3.8 workloads in fak
frame.problem: fragmentation can strand accelerator memory and cause late admission failures while live tensors fit
frame.today: treat OOM or shrinking capacity as aggregate pressure without a fragmentation ratio
frame.better_because: separate reserved, live, reusable, and stranded bytes can drive an owned mitigation without conflating IR with lifetime
frame.witness: a fak-native Qwen3.8 churn receipt compares reserved/live bytes, fragmentation, throughput, quality, admission, and recovery

p1_context.reason: accounting must not evict useful KV state or duplicate residency

p2_net_value.reason: witness counts overhead, reclaimed capacity, throughput, quality, and retries

p3_adaptation.reason: allocator policy stays behind a bounded reversible seam

p4_operations.reason: operators receive ratios, thresholds, refusal, and recovery

witness.pass_condition: bounded fragmentation with equal quality, net-true capacity/throughput, and recovery

candidates.title: Lower fak-native Qwen3.8 execution through a stable vLLM-IR-shaped optimization seam
candidates.merge_justification: the three architecture-runtime rules and the kernels-compilation label name one vLLM-IR boundary between model execution and compiled kernel lowering; one candidate retains all four rule-specific mappings while avoiding four incompatible IR contracts

hard_gates.name: bounded-source-coverage
hard_gates.evidence: four retained vLLM-IR inputs; allocator fragmentation remains distinct

hard_gates.name: semantic-merge-integrity
hard_gates.evidence: all four inputs normalize to one execution-to-kernel IR boundary with distinct cluster/rule/checksum mappings

hard_gates.name: fak-native-execution
hard_gates.evidence: execution, lowering, scheduling, cache, memory, and kernels remain fak-owned

hard_gates.name: qwen3.8-default
hard_gates.evidence: default implementation and quality envelope use Qwen3.8

hard_gates.name: end-to-end-witness
hard_gates.evidence: fak-native serve receipt covers quality, latency, memory, counters, and rollback

hard_gates.name: no-llama.cpp-fallback
hard_gates.evidence: llama.cpp is reference/borrow evidence only, never fallback

frame.for: operators running Qwen3.8 through fak-native inference
frame.problem: runtime and kernel optimizations lack one stable inspectable IR seam
frame.today: add one-off execution or kernel paths and use external engines only as references
frame.better_because: one owned IR contract unlocks repeated fak-native graph and kernel optimizations while preserving product ownership
frame.witness: a Qwen3.8 fak-native serve receipt names the IR lowering, matches accepted-token quality, reports net-true latency/memory, and proves rollback

p1_context.reason: the IR seam must not duplicate prompt, KV, or scheduler state

p2_net_value.reason: net-true evidence includes lowering, verification, and recovery cost

p3_adaptation.reason: a versioned bounded IR supports replaceable transforms and rollback

p4_operations.reason: the real serve receipt exposes selection, counters, refusal, and rollback

witness.pass_condition: equal accepted-token quality with net-true improvement, named engine, IR counters, and rollback
